title: The hidden factory
sub: The first film of Quality as a habit, the second series of Data quality: two people put the graduation list's names right by hand before every ceremony, in a copy, and the same errors come back every year. The team counts that hidden work, three ways, asks why five times, draws every cause on a fishbone, and fixes each one where the names are born, with checks that hold a doubt for a person and stop a night that loses letters.
howto: The film is drawn in the module's look: the data team's workroom, a wall of warm limestone and a granite bench, light from a window on the right. Green is a check that passes, amber a name held for a person to look at, red a check that stops the update, grey what nobody checked. Brass is what good means for this use, such as a name as its owner writes it, and steel blue a measure taken. Washington in 1899, 1943 and 1963 is painted full-frame, with the place and year on a tag.
